heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Polymaker PolyLite PETG reliably out of the box on its open-frame architecture with the stock stainless steel nozzle. By capping the maximum volumetric flow rate to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer, the system reaches a safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s while maintaining excellent layer adhesion and minimal stringing.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s under Filament Settings > Advanced to enforce the 167 mm/s speed ceiling for consistent melt flow.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a 2 mm wipe distance to prevent filament accumulation on the stock stainless steel nozzle tip.
Lower Part Cooling Fan settings to 20% minimum and 50% maximum, keeping auxiliary cooling off to maximize inter-layer adhesion.
Set the Pressure Advance value to roughly 0.038 (calibrated via OrcaSlicer line/pattern test) to eliminate seam oozing and corner bulge.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair-like wisps between travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and absorbed ambient moisture, paired with excessive nozzle temperature or travel unretracted.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours; in OrcaSlicer, enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' and set retraction to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Build plate surface damage or chunks torn out of PEI sheet
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically bonds too aggressively to smooth or unconditioned PEI surfaces upon cooling.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue as a sacrificial release agent before starting the print.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Delamination or brittle layer separation under mechanical load
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extruded bead before molecular fusion occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce cooling fan speeds to a 20-40% operational window and increase nozzle printing temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyLite PETG on the P1P without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG prints exceptionally well in open-frame environments because it does not suffer from aggressive thermal shrinkage like ABS or ASA.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle to print PolyLite PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard PolyLite PETG is non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel nozzle on the P1P completely sufficient for long-term printing.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at 167 mm/s?
faq.answer: The maximum volumetric flow rate of PolyLite PETG in the stock P1P hotend is 14 mm³/s, which mathematically limits safe line extrusion to 167 mm/s at standard 0.2mm layer heights.

faq.question: Is drying PolyLite PETG mandatory before feeding it into the P1P?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG absorbs moisture rapidly, leading to bubbling, degraded structural strength, and heavy stringing if not dried at 65°C before use.
